title: Acoustic delivery of indocyanine green via biosynthetic gas vesicles for tumor photothermal therapy
experiments_summary:
1. GV Biosynthesis and ICG-GV Fabrication: Halobacterium NRC-1 was cultured, lysed, and centrifuged to isolate GVs. ICG was conjugated to GV surface amino groups via amide bond formation by incubating ICG-NHS with GVs at 4°C, followed by purification via centrifugation and ultrafiltration.

2. Physicochemical Characterization: Particle size and zeta potential were measured using a Malvern Zetasizer. UV-VIS spectroscopy confirmed ICG conjugation. TEM was used to examine morphology before and after laser irradiation. Photostability was assessed by repeated 808 nm laser on-off cycling (5 cycles, 3 min on/10 min off).

3. In Vitro Multimodal Imaging: ICG-GVs at varying concentrations were placed in agarose phantoms and imaged by contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS; Mindray Resona 7, 3–11 MHz), photoacoustic (PA; VevoLAZR), and near-infrared fluorescence (NIRF) imaging systems.

4. In Vitro Photothermal Performance: ICG-GVs at varying ICG concentrations (10–40 μg/mL) were irradiated with an 808 nm laser at multiple power levels (0.5–1.25 W/cm²) for 3–5 min; temperature changes were recorded with an infrared camera.

5. Cell Culture and Tumor Model: MB49 murine bladder cancer cells were cultured in DMEM. Subcutaneous tumors were established in female C57BL/6 mice by injecting 4×10⁶ MB49 cells.

6. In Vitro Cytotoxicity and PTT Efficacy: MB49 cells in 96-well plates were divided into six groups (control, ICG-GVs, ICG-GVs+US, ICG-GVs+Laser, US+Laser, ICG-GVs+US+Laser). Pulsed ultrasound was applied for 1 min and/or 808 nm laser at 0.75 W/cm² for 5 min. Cell viability was assessed by CCK-8 assay. Live/dead staining with Calcein-AM/PI was performed for visual assessment. ICG-GV cytotoxicity alone was evaluated at multiple ICG concentrations.

7. In Vitro Acoustic ICG Delivery: MB49 cells were incubated with ICG-GVs and subjected to acoustic bursts every 10 s for 1 min; intracellular ICG uptake was visualized by fluorescence microscopy.

8. Pharmacokinetic Assessment: Healthy mice received intravenous injection of free ICG or ICG-GVs (ICG dose: 2 mg/kg); blood samples were collected at multiple time points to measure plasma ICG concentration and calculate half-life and AUC.

9. In Vivo Multimodal Imaging and Acoustic Delivery: Tumor-bearing mice received tail vein injection of ICG-GVs (OD500=3.0, ICG=40 μg/mL). CEUS imaging monitored tumor perfusion; acoustic power bursts (−3 dB) were applied every 10 s until GVs disappeared. NIRF imaging was performed at 0.5, 2, 4, 8, and 12 h post-injection to track ICG biodistribution and tumor accumulation across groups.

10. In Vivo Photothermal Temperature Measurement: Tumor-bearing mice in ICG-GVs+US+Laser and ICG-GVs+Laser groups received intravenous ICG-GVs with or without prior acoustic irradiation, followed by 808 nm laser irradiation; tumor surface temperatures were recorded by FTIR thermal camera.

11. In Vivo Anti-Tumor Efficacy: Tumor-bearing mice (n=8/group) were divided into six groups and treated as described. Tumor volumes and body weights were measured every two days. Survival was monitored until tumor volume reached 2,000 mm³ or death; Kaplan-Meier survival curves were generated.

12. Histological and Biosafety Analyses: Tumors and major organs (heart, liver, spleen, lung, kidney) were harvested, fixed, paraffin-embedded, sectioned, and stained with H&E for toxicity assessment. TUNEL assay was performed on tumor sections to assess apoptosis. Hematology markers and serum biochemical indicators of liver and kidney function were also evaluated.

13. Statistical Analysis: Data were analyzed using GraphPad Prism and SPSS. Normality was assessed by Shapiro-Wilk or Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests. Two-group comparisons used unpaired t-test or Mann-Whitney U test. Multi-group comparisons used one-way ANOVA with Tukey's post-hoc or Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn's test. Tumor growth curves used two-way repeated measures ANOVA with Sidak's correction. Survival curves used Kaplan-Meier with log-rank test.
